### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f770d664b84d1812f2de8f2c5f1b2bc6c2ca54cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `86dfdb7fd20c372aebceddf786ccb7a067e7dd99` — the merge of head `f81138926c0c11f7afc2e921105d1d01431485eb` into base `f770d664b84d1812f2de8f2c5f1b2bc6c2ca54cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 86dfdb7fd20c372aebceddf786ccb7a067e7dd99 && git checkout 86dfdb7fd20c372aebceddf786ccb7a067e7dd99
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f770d664b84d1812f2de8f2c5f1b2bc6c2ca54cb f81138926c0c11f7afc2e921105d1d01431485eb && git checkout -B drift-repro f770d664b84d1812f2de8f2c5f1b2bc6c2ca54cb && git merge --no-ff f81138926c0c11f7afc2e921105d1d01431485eb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f770d664b84d1812f2de8f2c5f1b2bc6c2ca54cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f770d664b84d1812f2de8f2c5f1b2bc6c2ca54cb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3f2b78433b095ec330eeca9062b7764faa733ed8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + none

Read for this record: card #32623 with all six comments (dev report 6820150398, release 6822991810), the PR body, the 13-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the 67 check-runs on this head (57 success, 10 skipped, none failed or pending). The 11 `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts` lines and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT; they are read here only for ② and for the registry header's own maintenance rule.

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff is one list member plus four jsdoc lines in `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai-studio']`. `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedToolName` are derived from the map (`Object.values(...).flat()`), so nothing else in the file needs a matching edit.
- The in-repo pin `platform-tool-names.test.ts` holds for the new name by reading: snake_case, no second group carries it (`get_record` in `service-ai` is a different name), it does not start with the `action_` family prefix, and it sits in sorted position between `get_package` and `list_metadata`. `Test Core` is green on this head.
- The header's second duty (a `chatbot.tool.NAME` label in every pack) is met: all 11 packs under `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/` on `main` gain the key; `Test UI` (16 shards) is green, which includes the parity suite that reads this registry.
- Consumers on `main`, read not reviewed: `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts:145` (the tool universe gains the name, so the warning-severity finding stops for a skill naming it) and `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts:451` (`worldAnnotation` now answers `openWorldHint: false` for a bridged tool of this name). No other hand copy of the list exists on `main`: a grep for a sibling member (`remove_sample_data`) finds only the registry, the locale packs and chat-card code that is specific to that tool.
- Not verifiable from here: `objectstack-ai/cloud` is not readable in this session (the API answers 403 for cloud#4374), so that the cloud registers `get_record_history`, that `service-ai-studio` is the package registering it, that it only reads, and that the restore goes through a confirm card are all carried from the card (filed by the cloud seat), not measured. The placement follows the precedent of `open_record` and `create_record` (chat-agent tools already in this group), and a wrong group fails the cloud conformance test at the pin bump, so the error is loud, not silent.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes` holds. The dev's measurement is right: the declared type is a readonly record of string to readonly string array, so declaration bytes do not move; what widens is the published runtime value, and two published consumers change their answer on it (lint universe, MCP world hint). The precedent changeset on `main` for the same kind of edit (`cloud-3565-spec-record-write-tool-names.md`) declared `no`; `yes` is the more cautious reading and is the one this review was owed for. Keep it.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds, so `patch` on both packages is the level owed. The one argument for `added` ("a new accepted value") fails on the code: `skill.tools[]` is a string array that parses any name before and after, and the registry feeds only a warning-severity lint finding (`validate-ai-tool-references.ts:23`, `:226`). What a metadata author can write does not change. The cloud-3565 precedent graded the same way, and `Check Changeset` is green.
- `@object-ui/i18n` patch for 11 added label strings: correct, additive.
- nit (prose face, the seat's ACCEPT): the changeset body ends "Nothing existing changes" and names the lint effect only. The MCP bridge effect (`openWorldHint: false` for this name, `mcp-server-runtime.ts:451`) is in the PR body but not in the text that ships as CHANGELOG. No effect on level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question, `PLATFORM_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts:258`): **A holds — leave it as is in this PR.** Evidence on `main`:
  - The set is "the last-resort fallback ... and deliberately NOT a general classifier" (`:208`) and "deliberately partial: they carry only the platform names whose safety class this bridge knows" (`:395-396`). It lists five names; the registry already carries about a dozen read-shaped names outside it (`get_package`, `list_metadata`, `describe_metadata`, `get_metadata_schema`, `get_authoring_rules`, `list_packages`, `search_knowledge`, `query_data`, ...). Absence is the existing norm, not a gap this PR opens.
  - Omission is the conservative direction: a tool with no source gets no hint (`safetyAnnotations` returns an empty object), and the MCP default for a missing `readOnlyHint` is "not read-only" (`:329-334`). The cost is information and possibly a host prompt before a read, never safety.
  - No pin goes red. Both pins hold the sets as a SUBSET of the registry (`mcp-tool-bridge-safety-annotations.test.ts:299` and the sibling describe at `:448-475`); neither requires every read-only registry name to be in the set.
  - Adding the name would make this repo promise "read-only" by name for a tool whose behaviour cannot be read from here (see ①). That is the unsourced claim the file's header exists to stop.
- One correction to the dev's reasoning, not to the recommendation: the header does not say the tool definition should source `readOnlyHint`. It says the opposite: "There is no declared source for it at all: `AIToolDefinition` has no member expressing 'this tool only reads'" (`:329-331`). So B is not owed by this card; if the hint is wanted, it is an `mcp` lane card, best filed after the cloud tool is landed and its definition can be read, and the durable fix is the declared member the header names as the follow-up, not a sixth literal.
- Cross-repo order: this lands first, cloud#4374 then needs the pin bump. Until the cloud ships the tool, a skill naming `get_record_history` passes lint against a runtime that may not register it; the runtime tolerates unresolved names by design (`validate-ai-tool-references.ts:25-27`), so this is the normal order, flagged only.
- Docs drift bot names `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx` as touching the symbol; it is release-owned and correctly untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts` — holds. Attempts to break it:

- Collision or shadowing: `get_record_history` shares a prefix with `service-ai`'s `get_record`, but every reader does exact `Set.has` membership; no prefix match exists outside `PLATFORM_TOOL_FAMILY_PREFIXES`, which is `action_` only.
- Name squatting: a stack or plugin that already registered its own `get_record_history` now gets `openWorldHint: false` from the bridge by name. Same exposure every registry name already has, and the stack's own `stack.tools[]` name resolved in lint before the registry anyway. No new class.
- Group contract ("each group is the exact set that package registers"): the module header maps the `ask` product to `service-ai`, and this `ask` tool lands in `service-ai-studio`. The jsdoc states it openly and matches `open_record`; whether it is exact is the cloud conformance test's verdict (see ①). Not a finding from here.
- nit: the group jsdoc states three cloud behaviours as fact (read-only, limited to history the user may see, restore behind a confirm card) from a repository a reader of this file cannot open. Sibling sentences in the same comment do the same; `build-progress.zod.ts:30-42` shows the house way of marking such claims as carried. Wording only.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix, 2 nit (changeset omits the MCP world-hint effect; jsdoc carries unverifiable cloud behaviour as fact). Nits are accepted deviations or a prose-face edit; neither needs a new head.

**VERDICT: PASS**

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；

> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
